title: Disability Accommodations Elimination in Higher Education - University Access Destruction
description_short: Disability Accommodations Elimination in Higher Education - University Access Destruction
description_medium: Disability-rights organizations warned that Project 2025 could undermine protections and access for disabled students. Their analyses discuss proposed policy changes and potential consequences for students at colleges across the country. They do not establish that Trump abolished university accommodations, accessibility offices or statutory duties under the Americans with Disabilities Act.
organization_tags: Disability Rights Education and Defense Fund
American Association of People with Disabilities

preserved_fields.title: Disability Accommodations Elimination in Higher Education - University Access Destruction
preserved_fields.description_short: Disability Accommodations Elimination in Higher Education - University Access Destruction

notes: The linked disability-rights analyses discuss risks associated with Project 2025 proposals, not a repeal of ADA accommodations or a ban on university accessibility programs. The existing long description asserts completed actions and legal violations that the supplied sources do not establish. A specific enacted measure is needed to support the title.
proposed_correction: Disability Advocates Warn Project 2025 Could Threaten Student Access and Rights

title: Trump: Michael Caputo uses dirty tactics as campaign manager for New York real estate mogul
description_short: Trump: Michael Caputo uses dirty tactics as campaign manager for New York real estate mogul
description_medium: In 2010, Michael Caputo managed Carl Paladino’s New York gubernatorial campaign after Roger Stone recommended him. The linked timeline describes attack ads against Democratic rival Andrew Cuomo, including a fabricated image showing Cuomo shirtless and covered in mud. Its claim that the tactics were later used by Trump’s campaign is not documented in the supplied excerpt.
description_long: Michael Caputo became campaign manager for Carl Paladino’s 2010 campaign for governor of New York after Roger Stone recommended him, according to the linked Trumpfile timeline. The page describes the campaign’s aggressive attacks on Paladino’s Democratic rival, Andrew Cuomo. It says Caputo wrote nicknames for Cuomo and produced attack advertisements, including one that used a fabricated image of the attorney general shirtless in a shower and covered in mud to portray him as a corrupt politician. The timeline also says that methods from the Paladino campaign were later used by Donald Trump’s campaign, but the excerpt provides no examples showing which tactics were repeated or how the connection was established. The reported ad is a concrete example of the campaign’s negative messaging; it does not by itself demonstrate a transfer of methods to a later campaign. The supplied title’s broader Trump connection needs evidence beyond this episode.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Michael Caputo uses dirty tactics as campaign manager for New York real estate mogul
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Michael Caputo uses dirty tactics as campaign manager for New York real estate mogul

notes: The exact linked Trumpfile page was read directly and cites a New York Times report on Caputo’s attack advertising. It supports the Paladino campaign role and the Cuomo image ad, but not the title’s claim that Trump’s campaign later reused those tactics. Proposed correction narrows the entry to the documented 2010 campaign.
proposed_correction: Michael Caputo Runs Carl Paladino’s 2010 New York Campaign With Attack Ads

title: Trump: Paul Manafort helps in the Russian takeover of Ukraine
description_short: Trump: Paul Manafort helps in the Russian takeover of Ukraine
description_medium: The linked Trumpfile timeline says Russia seized Crimea in 2014 and asserts that Paul Manafort helped the Kremlin, but does not describe what he did. The cited Vox explainer covers the Ukraine crisis and Crimea referendum; it does not support the claimed Manafort role or a connection to Donald Trump in this event.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Paul Manafort helps in the Russian takeover of Ukraine
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Paul Manafort helps in the Russian takeover of Ukraine

title: Trump: Russian social media accounts start spreading Trump propaganda
description_short: Trump: Russian social media accounts start spreading Trump propaganda
description_medium: A Trumpfile timeline says some social-media accounts that had promoted Russian actions in Ukraine shifted to pro-Trump messages in December 2015. It attributes the observation to a journalist who studies the Internet Research Agency and links a 2017 U.S. intelligence assessment. The account names no specific profiles or evidence tying their operators to Russia.

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Russian social media accounts start spreading Trump propaganda

title: Trump campaign adviser meets with Kremlin official in Moscow, covers it up
description_short: Trump campaign adviser meets with Kremlin official in Moscow, covers it up
description_medium: Carter Page met Russian officials during a 2016 Moscow trip, including Deputy Prime Minister Arkady Dvorkovich and Rosneft figures, according to the linked timeline. Page later gave differing accounts of what meetings took place and who in the campaign knew about the trip. The record does not establish that those discrepancies amounted to a cover-up.
description_long: The linked Trumpfile timeline says Carter Page, then a Trump campaign foreign-policy adviser, traveled to Moscow in 2016 and met Deputy Prime Minister Arkady Dvorkovich, Rosneft investor-relations head Andrey Baranov and Rosneft chief Igor Sechin. It also says Page met Igor Diveykin, though Page denied meeting Sechin or Diveykin. The timeline describes changes in Page’s account of who knew about the trip: initially he said no one in the campaign knew, then that staff learned after he returned, and later he told the House Intelligence Committee that J.D. Gordon, Corey Lewandowski, Hope Hicks and Jeff Sessions knew beforehand. Page reportedly emailed Trump officials afterward with a “readout” of insights from Russian officials. These are the timeline’s account of the meetings and later disclosures, with some claims attributed to Christopher Steele or Page himself. They show why the trip drew scrutiny, but the page alone does not establish that Page concealed the meetings or prove campaign coordination with Russia.

preserved_fields.title: Trump campaign adviser meets with Kremlin official in Moscow, covers it up
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump campaign adviser meets with Kremlin official in Moscow, covers it up

notes: The linked Trumpfile page was read directly. It recounts Page’s meetings and changing statements about campaign awareness, but mixes his accounts with Christopher Steele’s reporting and does not independently establish a cover-up or campaign coordination. Proposed correction describes the trip and evolving disclosures without asserting concealment.
proposed_correction: Carter Page’s Moscow Meetings and Changing Accounts of Campaign Awareness
